title: TAA bugfixes and improvements

milestone.title: 4.x
milestone.description: Issues and pull requests slated for an undetermined Godot 4 release.

body:
## What problem(s) does this PR solve? Our current TAA implementation is low quality and artifact prone. Partially fixes #81709 Alternative to #121368 ## Additional information This PR contains several minor bugfixes for the current TAA implementation I came up with when comparing the TAA shader with references. There are several more things that could be changed and improved (e.g. passing an alpha mask to TAA, so we can weigh the current frame more heavily, ~look into ping ponging the buffers~(done) ...), but I still consider this PR a step forward, and a good bandaid until someone finally takes the time to completely overhaul it. #### Velocity Dilation On master our TAA had a tendency to mess up the edges of meshes when either the mesh itself or the camera was moving. The widely accepted solution for this is dilating the motion vectors, something we already did. However, for some reason dilated motion vectors were only used for neighbourhood clipping. Using dilated motion vectors for everything (matching the current state of the art) fixed those artifacts. #### Anti Flicker The luminance anti flicker code could re-enable history blending, even after we already disabled it due to occlusion. Applying `factor_screen + factor_disocclusion` after anti flicker fixed this. #### Neighbourhood Clipping For some reason we were doing this in rgb, when pretty much everyone recommends using ycocg. We now need a couple more ALU operations, but the quality improvement is significant. While I was at it I also removed the dynamic box sizing base don velocity. The problem was that in motion this collapsed the box down to 0, which made neighbourhood clipping redundant. I also couldn't find any precedent for other engines doing someething similar. After playing around with the shader a bit I decided to simply remove this. If we want to add something similar in the future the proper solution would probably be to increase the weight of the current frame when the velocity vectors are big. ## Screenshots Here are screenshots of my testing scene. Note that the fox is skinned. Both the fox and the lamp post are moving towards the camera, while the helmet is motionless. Furthermore, the camera is moving from the left to the right.

I recommend using https://www.diffchecker.com/image-compare/ to compare the images. Both the slider and the subtract view are very useful. ## TODO (maybe, most of this is trial and error) - [x] play with reset factors, maybe add depth based. Intel uses a bunch and we already have all the necessary data available - we did not have all the data necessary for depth diocclusion. Still adjusted logic slightly to have less aliasing for the first frame a pixel is visible by blending in local avg. - [x] change shape of neighbouhood clip. Unreal recommends combining the 3x3 box with a plus shape to add additional weight to the center, should be trivial. - [x] don't like the border between skybox and geometry when moving, I suspect the velocity dilation is a bit too aggressive. Maybe add a simple depth check to handle this case. - [x] look at the neighbourhood clipping logic, at a glance it looks different to what I have seen other people use. - just replaced it with the slab method. afaik thats the state of the art for AABB intersections. - [x] ~traditionally TAA is followed by either a sharpen pass, or uses some kind of sharpening internally. Look into that.~ - not happy with the result. Will look into this some more in the future, out of scope for now. - [x] sanity check performance ## References https://www.elopezr.com/temporal-aa-and-the-quest-for-the-holy-trail/ (+ anything linked here!) https://de45xmedrsdbp.cloudfront.net/Resources/files/TemporalAA_small-59732822.pdf#page=30 https://developer.download.nvidia.com/gameworks/events/GDC2016/msalvi_temporal_supersampling.pdf https://github.com/GameTechDev/TAA EDIT: all of the code in this PR was written by me. I did let claude write a gdscript to capture and store the current framebuffer, which I used in my testing projects to capture screenshots at identical frames in order to compare them.
